q_45367.question_text: What will be NVIDIA's forward guidance in its Q2 FY2027 earnings release? (Revenue)
q_45367.reasoning:
# Analysis of NVIDIA's Q2 FY2027 Forward Guidance (Revenue)

## (a) Time left until resolution
The earnings release is tomorrow, August 26, 2026. Resolution is imminent — less than 24 hours.

## (b) Most likely outcome and why

The question asks for NVIDIA's **forward guidance** issued during the Q2 FY2027 earnings release tomorrow. This is critical: the question is NOT asking about Q2 FY2027 actual results (which will be reported), but rather what guidance NVIDIA will issue for **subsequent quarters**.

Key facts from research:
- NVIDIA's current Q2 FY2027 guidance (issued in May) is $91.0B ±2%, or $89.2B–$92.8B
- Wall Street consensus for Q2 FY2027 actual results: $91.9B (42 analyst estimates)
- Q1 FY2027 actual revenue: $81.6B (record)
- BofA and others are discussing potential Q3 guidance of $107–$108B (vs. $104B consensus)

The question range provided is 99.5–115.5 billion. This range makes sense for **forward guidance** because:
- It spans well above the current Q2 guidance of ~$91B
- It encompasses the Q3 guidance being discussed ($107–$108B range)
- It allows for acceleration from Q1 ($81.6B) → Q2 (~$91B) → Q3 ($107–$110B range)

NVIDIA has shown consistent sequential growth and typically provides guidance for the next quarter. Given the BofA commentary about Q3 guidance of $107–$108B, the most likely outcome is that tomorrow's earnings will include forward guidance (for Q3 FY2027) in the **$105–$110B range**, with a midpoint around **$107–$108B**.

## (c) What would push the value lower?

- Weaker demand signals or AI spending slowdown not yet fully reflected
- Geopolitical headwinds intensifying (though China revenue exclusion is already assumed)
- Competitive pressures from AMD or others materializing faster than expected
- Macro weakness reducing enterprise capex commitments
- Conservative management guidance relative to analyst expectations

## (d) What would push the value higher?

- Stronger-than-expected demand from hyperscalers (OpenAI, Google, Meta, Microsoft)
- Better-than-expected gross margins providing pricing power
- Accelerated AI adoption across industries beyond cloud
- Supply chain improvements enabling higher volumes than previously guided
- Analyst expectations like BofA's $107–$108B Q3 estimate being exceeded
- Continued data center strength offsetting any cloud softness

## (e) Base rate or historical reference values

From the research provided: BofA analysts discussing Q3 guidance of **$107–$108 billion** (vs. $104B consensus). This is the most concrete forward-looking anchor in the research. NVIDIA's recent quarterly growth (Q1: $81.6B → expected Q2: ~$91B) shows sequential growth of ~11–12%, which if continued to Q3 would suggest ~$101–$103B, but analyst commentary suggests higher at $107–$108B.

The range provided (99.5–115.5B) brackets expectations well. The BofA commentary of $107–$108B is the strongest signal available.

---

**Reasoning on distribution:**
- The BofA $107–$108B guidance estimate is the most specific forward indicator
- NVIDIA typically guides to achievable targets (tends to beat slightly)
- The lower bound of the range (99.5B) represents conservative scenarios
- The upper bound (115.5B) represents very bullish scenarios
- Given sequential growth patterns and analyst consensus clustering around $107–$108B, this should be the median region

The 10th percentile (substantially below consensus) would reflect disappointing guidance or demand signals: ~101–103B
The 50th percentile (consensus-aligned) should be around 107–108B per BofA
The 90th percentile (strong upside) would reflect better-than-expected demand: ~112–115B

q_45367.research_text:
NVIDIA is set to release its Q2 FY2027 earnings on August 26, 2026 [morningstar.com](https://www.morningstar.com/stocks/going-into-earnings-is-nvidia-stock-buy-sell-or-fairly-valued-8). For Q2 FY2027, NVIDIA's own guidance, issued in May, projects revenue of $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2% [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). This implies a revenue range of $89.2 billion to $92.8 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/).

Wall Street analysts, based on 42 estimates, anticipate an average of $91.9 billion [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). This figure falls within NVIDIA's guided range, about 1% above the midpoint [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). The guidance explicitly assumes no data center compute revenue from China [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/19/nvidia-guided-to-usd91-billion-wall-street-penciled-in-usd92-billion/). Gross margin is expected to be around 75% [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027). For Q1 FY2027, NVIDIA reported record revenue of $81.6 billion [nvidianews.nvidia.com](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-announces-financial-results-for-first-quarter-fiscal-2027). Some analysts, like BofA, are discussing a potential Q3 guide of $107–108 billion (vs. a $104 billion consensus) [streetsignal.substack.com](https://streetsignal.substack.com/p/nvda-earnings-bridge).
